newsitem.title: CANADA: Alcan hopeful for Kemano talks.
newsitem.headline: Alcan hopeful for Kemano talks.

text.p: Alcan Aluminium Ltd said on Monday that it was hopeful that negotiations would resume with the British Columbia government over compensation for the company's cancelled Kemano hydroelectric project.

The province said last week it was abandoning the talks after Alcan filed a court action over the case. Alcan said it wanted to continue negotiations and filed the lawsuit only to protect its legal right to sue if the talks ultimately failed.

Alcan president Jacques Bougie wrote to British Columbia Premier Glen Clark explaining that and assuring him that the legal action would not proceed any further, Alcan spokesman Ray Castelli said. The premier had since indicated that talks might resume, Castelli said.
"Premier Clark seems to have acknowledged that (Alcan) position. We are optimistic we can hopefully get back to the negotiating table," Castelli said.
Alcan said previously it hoped for more negotiations in February.

The provincial government and the company negotiated unsuccessfully for almost two years after the province in 1995 cancelled the half-built Kemano project in northern British Columbia on which Alcan had spent C$535 million.
